newsitem.title: USA: Who regulates U.S. holding firm in crisis?-Dingell.
newsitem.headline: Who regulates U.S. holding firm in crisis?-Dingell.

text.p: It was unclear under proposed financial services reform legislation which regulator would take the lead if one or more parts of a financial services holding company entered a crisis, Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt said Thursday.

"I think you've put your finger on a real problem because it's basically unclear what would happen in the event of such a failure under the proposed legislation," Levitt told a House Commerce subcommittee.
Michigan Democrat Rep. John Dingell had posed a scenario where banking, insurance and securities regulators would make competing demands when a firm failed.
"Who wins the tug of war and why?" Dingell asked.

Treasury undersecretary John Hawke said that if all aspects of a holding company were failing simultaneously then there would likely be enormous economic problems that went beyond the structure of financial institutions.
"I think that would be an enourmously difficult situation and I don't know the answer to that is in all honestly," Hawke said.
Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan agreed with Hawke that Dingell's scenario suggested the beginnings of a serious systemic financial crises.
Greenspan said it underlined the importance of having the Fed involved in regulating institutions that were big enough to create problems for others if they failed.
